pages.text:
Hello, nice to meet you!
My name is Bohlale.
I am nine years old.
How old are you?
pages.change: Bohlale introduces herself and asks the reader's age
pages.question_created: How old am I compared with her?
pages.page_turn_note: Direct question to the listener; low narrative pull

notes: Bohlale waves outside a market stall in front of a building; a speech bubble repeats her greeting

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
This is my family. I am the youngest and my Gogo is the oldest.
I have one brother. He is two years older than me. I also have a sister. She is three years older than my brother.
What are the ages of my brother and sister?
pages.change: Her family is introduced, youngest to oldest, with an age sum to work out
pages.page_turn_note: A maths question, not a story question

notes: Gogo, sister, Bohlale and brother walk in a line across grass, tallest to smallest

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
My siblings are allowed to go to the mountains to collect fruit, and to go to the river.
I would love to do those things as well. Everyone always tells me that I am too young, too small, too weak, and not brave enough yet.
pages.change: She wants to go where her siblings go but everyone says she is too young, small, weak and not brave enough

notes: the family at a table with mugs; Bohlale between her siblings and Gogo
illustration.only_in_image: At the table her siblings sit taller and she sits squeezed between them

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
I wish my family would believe in me!
Gogo comes into my room. She kisses me and says, "Goodnight."
Then she whispers in my ear, "Always remember that I believe in you."
pages.change: Gogo says goodnight and whispers that she believes in her
pages.question_created: What will happen in the night?
pages.page_turn_note: Bedtime frame opens; the starry window marks night

notes: night sky full of stars in the window; Bohlale lies on a mattress, Gogo standing beside her

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
I fall asleep. In my dream, I find a message in a bottle. The message is:
"If you want to be brave, follow the map to the highest mountain. There you will find a special drink.
One sip of that drink will make you the bravest girl in the world."
pages.change: In a dream she finds a message promising a bravery drink at the top of the highest mountain

notes: a dream bubble holding a hand-drawn map with a dotted route to a mountain

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
I am not as wise as my Gogo. I am not as strong as my brother nor as brave as my sister.
But if I find this drink, then I will be able to do anything.
Help me to follow the map, count 50 steps straight ahead.
1, 2, 3,
pages.change: She sets out to find the drink and asks the reader to count steps with her; the count breaks off at three
pages.page_turn_note: The count is cut mid-way and resumes at 47 on the next page: the reader counts across the turn

notes: Bohlale walks with the map beside a blue river among acacia trees

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
47, 48, 49, 50 steps!
Oh no, a river! How will I make it to the other side? I think I will give up because I cannot swim.
Look at that leaf floating on the water!
I have got an idea.
pages.action: blocked by river, gets an idea
pages.change: A river blocks her; she nearly gives up, then a floating leaf gives her an idea
pages.page_turn_note: Ends on 'I have an idea' without saying what it is

notes: Bohlale at the riverbank with a question mark over her head; a leaf drifts down from a tree

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
I can build a raft!
Here are five tree branches. How many more branches do I need to build a raft with eleven branches?
After building the raft, I can cross the river without swimming. Where will I go next?
pages.change: She builds a raft and crosses without swimming

notes: Bohlale with arms raised and a light bulb above her; branches around her and a finished raft

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
After 100 steps, I think am lost! Where is the mountain?
I will never find the way to the highest mountain. I think I have to give up because I am too small.
pages.change: She is lost and thinks of giving up because she is too small
pages.question_created: How will she find the mountain?
pages.page_turn_note: The picture already holds the answer (the giraffe)

notes: Bohlale with a question mark beside an acacia tree; a giraffe eats leaves from it
illustration.only_in_image: A giraffe is feeding at the tree beside her before the text mentions it: the picture plants the next solution

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
The giraffe can see the mountain because it is very tall.
If I climb this tree, I will be as tall as a giraffe!
I can see how far away the mountain is.
pages.change: Copying the giraffe, she climbs the tree and sees how far the mountain is

notes: Bohlale at the top of the acacia pointing at a small far mountain; the giraffe's head beside the tree
illustration.only_in_image: The mountain is a tiny shape far off, showing the distance the text only mentions

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
I climb down from the tree.
After 200 steps, I am at the foot of the highest mountain.
There is a cave, with scary eyes looking at me!
I think I will give up because I am afraid.
pages.location: dream: cave at the mountain foot
pages.change: At the mountain foot a cave holds scary eyes; she thinks of giving up because she is afraid
pages.page_turn_note: Strongest turn: the threat is left unexplained across the page turn

notes: a dark cave mouth with many pairs of yellow eyes; Bohlale points at it

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Look again carefully, those scary eyes are only fireflies.
The fireflies could help to guide me through the cave to the top of the mountain.
pages.change: Looking again, the eyes are fireflies, and they can guide her through the cave

notes: Bohlale smiling among glowing green fireflies with big eyes
illustration.only_in_image: The fireflies are drawn with big friendly eyes, turning the threat into helpers

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Here I am at the top of the mountain!
How many steps did I walk in total?
I can see the special drink of bravery! I am going to drink it now.
pages.change: She reaches the top, sees the drink and is about to drink it
pages.page_turn_note: The page stops just before she drinks

notes: Bohlale with arms spread on top of the rocky mountain above the cave; a glowing green bottle

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
"Good moooorning!" says Gogo.
I wake up suddenly!
"Gogo, I had a dream." I tell Gogo about the message and my journey.
"I am still not as wise as you. I am still not as strong as my brother nor as brave as my sister."
pages.change: Gogo's good-morning wakes her before she drinks; she tells the dream and still feels not wise, strong or brave enough
pages.page_turn_note: The dream is cut off; the missing sip creates the question

notes: same bedroom as page 4, now with a sunrise in the window
illustration.only_in_image: The same bedroom as page 4, now with a sunrise: the frame closes visually

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Gogo smiles and says, "Are you telling me that you are not brave enough? How did you get to the highest mountain? How did you walk through the cave?
You do not need that special drink, because you ARE brave!"
pages.change: Gogo points out that she crossed the river and the cave herself, so she is already brave

notes: Gogo smiling, Bohlale waving beside her

pages.label: OBSERVED
